llm.summary: This skill coherently provides a disclosed, API-backed presentation generation workflow, with document upload and billing risks that users should understand before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill uploads user-provided materials to the documented AI Skills API and may incur per-use fees, which is proportionate to the cloud presentation-generation purpose and disclosed in the docs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation requires curl and a configured AI Skills API key in OpenClaw environment settings; no executable package scripts or local code payloads were present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions require staged execution, user review of the outline before file generation, bounded layouts/themes, source citation preservation, and separate authorization before publishing or sending externally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The API key persists in OpenClaw config and platform tasks/files are described as user-isolated with seven-day expiry; no system services, background agents, local persistence hooks, or privilege escalation were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to turn briefs or documents into editable presentations with source references, and the documented inspect, outline, and generate API steps directly support that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending the selected source material to the AI Skills service and paying the documented API charges. Use a product-specific key if you want tighter separation, avoid pasting full keys into chat, and review generated outlines and files before sharing them externally.
llm.findings:
[SQP-3] unexpected: The artifact and references are Chinese-only, which may limit user understanding, but this does not hide unrelated capabilities or create a security mismatch in the inspected materials.
[E1] expected: The external POST requests send presentation inputs to the documented AI Skills API endpoint using the configured API key; this is disclosed and central to the skill's function, not evidence of covert exfiltration.
